Noise transition matrices and class priors

Source: R/joint.R
noise_matrices.Rd

Derives from the estimated joint (see estimate_joint()) the quantities used to characterise label noise (Northcutt et al., 2021, Sec. 3.1). Both matrices are oriented with given labels in rows and true labels in columns.

Usage

noise_matrices(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Labels or an object holding labels and predicted probabilities. See Description.

...

Passed to label_inputs(): for example pred_probs when x is a label vector, or truth when x is a data frame.

Value

A list with

  • joint: the estimated joint distribution P(given = i, true = j).

  • prior_given: observed class proportions P(given = i).

  • prior_true: estimated true class proportions P(true = j).

  • noise_matrix: P(given = i | true = j); columns sum to one. The diagonal is the probability that an example of class j keeps its label.

  • inverse_noise_matrix: P(true = j | given = i); rows sum to one. The diagonal is the probability that a label i is correct.

A class with an estimated true prior of zero has NA in its column of noise_matrix.

References

Northcutt, C., Jiang, L., & Chuang, I. (2021). Confident learning: Estimating uncertainty in dataset labels. Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research, 70, 1373–1411. doi:10.1613/jair.1.12125

Examples

sim <- simulate_label_noise(n = 500, seed = 1)
nm <- noise_matrices(sim, truth = given)
round(nm$inverse_noise_matrix, 2)
#>      true
#> given    A    B    C    D
#>     A 0.87 0.04 0.03 0.06
#>     B 0.09 0.81 0.06 0.03
#>     C 0.07 0.07 0.82 0.04
#>     D 0.09 0.15 0.07 0.70
